symptom: An intermediate PR test commit serialized JavaScript Unicode escape sequences with two literal backslashes. The test therefore compared a literal backslash-u string rather than an unpaired surrogate against U+FFFD. Official CI verify failed one synthetic regression assertion (false !== true) while research-governance/typecheck passed; this was a fixture-construction error, not a research payload or runner failure.
lesson: When generating TypeScript test source from another JavaScript string, double escaping can accidentally turn a Unicode code-unit fixture into a literal backslash-u sequence. A green typecheck cannot detect a semantically wrong fixture; verify the exact emitted source and runtime bytes before relying on negative tests.
guardrail: For generated malformed UTF-16 fixtures, read back the emitted test source and confirm it contains one JavaScript Unicode escape before the u; assert Buffer UTF-8 equivalence against the U+FFFD counterpart and require the named regression to execute in CI. Distinguish test-fixture assertion failure, process exit 1, workflow failure, successful post-job cleanup and healthy runner state. Do not attribute this failure to the research digest implementation.
